objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a patient presenting with sudden, unilateral loss of vision.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“About 30 minutes ago I suddenly lost vision in my right eye while I was watching TV. It was painless and there’s been no change in my left eye since then.”
Can you describe exactly what you're seeing in the right eye right now—is it completely black, blurry/gray, or does it feel like a dark curtain or shadow covering part of your vision?
“It’s like a dark curtain that covered part of my right vision, and the rest is pretty blurry/gray—my eye isn’t completely black. It’s painless, and the left eye still seems normal.”
Did you notice any new flashes of light, a sudden increase in floaters, or a "shower of spots" in that eye right before or when the vision loss started?
“No, I didn’t notice any flashes of light or a sudden increase in floaters or a shower of spots right before it happened.”
How old are you, and do you have any history of high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, smoking, or heart rhythm problems like atrial fibrillation?

“I’m 60 years old. I have high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, coronary artery disease, and I smoke about 10 cigarettes a day; I also haven’t been fully consistent with my medications, and I don’t know of any atrial fibrillation.”
Is the vision loss staying exactly the same, getting progressively worse, or starting to improve since it began 30 minutes ago?
“It has stayed about the same since it started 30 minutes ago—neither fully improving nor clearly getting worse. I haven’t noticed any pain, and it’s only the right eye that’s affected.”
Does the dark curtain specifically cover the top half, bottom half, or one side of your vision?
“It covers the vision on one side of my right eye—like a dark curtain along that side—rather than specifically only the top or only the bottom.”
Have you experienced any new headaches, scalp tenderness, or pain in your jaw when chewing recently?
“No, I haven’t had any new headaches, scalp tenderness, or jaw pain when chewing. I also haven’t had any chest pain, dizziness, or trouble breathing.”
Have you noticed any new neurological symptoms such as facial drooping, arm or leg weakness, or difficulty speaking since this started?
“No, I haven’t noticed any facial drooping, arm or leg weakness, or trouble speaking—everything else feels normal besides the right-eye vision change.”
Have you experienced any similar brief episodes of temporary vision loss in either eye in the past, even if they resolved completely on their own?
“No, I haven’t had any similar brief episodes of temporary vision loss before—this is the first time it’s happened.”
[DDX] Branch Retinal Artery Occlusion, Central Retinal Artery Occlusion, Retinal Detachment, Non-arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy, Amaurosis Fugax
